summary: Independently re-derives HPAC-REQ-092's closed 8-field attestation schema from the contract text (not .3.2.2 source) and matches it exactly against production. Independently re-attacks the .3.2.2 canonical-store containment repair with a 10-vector absolute-path/traversal matrix plus symlink, cross-store-substitution, and canonical-root-placement-without-provenance attacks -- all rejected for the correct authority reasons. Fixed-SHA (git worktree) HPAC-family comparison finds exactly the 4 expected candidate-only failing nodes and zero unexplained regressions. Finding P: CLOSED. Finding C: CLOSED. Principal and proof-writer provenance remain independently closed. No repair applied (verification-only). Layer 3 not begun; no next-phase ID disclosed by canonical project state, so none invented.
derived_correctness: HPAC-REQ-092's exact eight-field closed schema was independently re-derived from docs/contracts/HUMAN_PRINCIPAL_AUTHENTICATION_CONTRACT.md section 39.2 (quoted in the phase doc), not inferred from .3.2.2's implementation or test module, then compared field-for-field against production's presentation_attestation_object(). The pre-repair absolute-path escape was reconstructed from Path.__truediv__'s documented behavior (discards the left operand when the right is absolute) and independently re-attacked post-repair with a 10-vector matrix across both HPACLifecycleStore and RuntimeInvocationAuthorityConsumptionStore; all 10 rejected before any file I/O. Two additional fresh tests (canonical-root-placement-without-provenance) were initially authored with an incorrect attack premise (rewriting identical bytes at an already-provenanced path is not a forgery); this was caught during authoring, corrected, and disclosed in the phase doc rather than silently fixed.
